# Summary

Trace RMED claims to canonical module owners

## Scope

The admitted PROGRAMMATIC implementation boundary, including its descendant
Tools, Apps, MCP components, workflows and policy implementations. Generated
output, vendor code, frozen fixtures and legacy history remain outside this
Requirement unless separately admitted.

## Claim

Every applicable active RMED claim realized inside the admitted boundary must
be discoverably traceable to the actual canonical source module or package
that materially owns its implementation. The trace must distinguish a genuine
owner from a facade, caller, dependency or other consumer that merely reuses
the behavior. A claim may have several genuine owners and an owner may realize
several claims; many-to-many realization is valid when each relationship is
substantive.

Unknown, dynamic or ambiguous realization must be reported as unresolved;
known unimplemented claims must be reported as unimplemented. Neither may be
converted into an invented owner, relationship or compliance result.
Trace metadata is evidence of where to
inspect; it is not proof that the implementation conforms, is complete, or
has produced the required outcome.

## Details

1. Establish the current applicable RMED claims and the admitted
   implementation boundary before assessing traceability. Resolve each claim
   to the actual source owner when the owner is identifiable; preserve an
   explicit uncertainty when it is not.
2. Keep the owner/consumer distinction visible. A module that only imports,
   calls, decorates or wraps another implementation is not its owner solely
   for that reuse. A module that independently materializes applicable
   behavior is a genuine owner even when another module supplies a shared
   policy.
3. Preserve independent branches and many-to-many relationships without
   claiming that a projection, comment, relation, generated artifact or test
   invocation alone owns the implementation. A test may be an owner of an
   Evaluation claim when it materially implements that evaluation, but merely
   exercising another module does not transfer ownership.
4. Report missing, stale, ambiguous or out-of-boundary traceability as an
   unresolved gap for explicit disposition. Do not mass-edit sources or infer
   proof from a missing or malformed trace.

This Draft states the required traceability outcome: discoverable ownership of
implemented RMED claims, honest unresolved reporting and no false compliance
proof. The companion Method Draft defines how module-level owner metadata is
written and how owner/provider/consumer relationships are derived. The
companion Evaluation Draft checks whether that Method is applied correctly.
Current CA-R-2117, CA-M-431, CA-E-653 and CA-M-411 remain active authority
until a reviewed role correction or replacement is accepted and promoted.
This Draft does not silently supersede them and is not an implementation or
release gate.

# Summary

Organize cohesive modules, packages and assets

## Scope

New or materially changed hand-authored PROGRAMMATIC implementation,
including code modules, packages, tests and owned non-code source assets
throughout descendant Scope Units. This Method owns the source-size,
cohesion, package-organization and source-asset rules; linked Evaluation
carriers measure and check them but do not own the policy.

## Claim

Organize implementation around cohesive responsibilities and the following
non-optional source boundaries:

- Every executable function and method has a 25-line soft limit and a
  40-line hard limit. Crossing the soft limit requires a cohesion review and
  written justification. More than 40 logical executable lines is a failure
  with no exception.
- Every module has a 200-line soft limit and a 300-line hard limit. Crossing
  200 physical lines requires a cohesion review and written justification.
  More than 300 physical lines is a failure with no exception.
- Logical executable function LOC excludes comments, docstrings and blank
  lines. Module physical LOC includes all text under the current counting
  convention.
- Each class has one cohesive responsibility and has no arbitrary numeric
  class-size cap. Every method defined on a class remains governed by the
  function and method limits.
- A helper is meaningful only when it expresses a reusable responsibility or
  boundary. Do not add helpers, wrappers, indirection, line compression or
  formatting changes merely to game a threshold.
- Growing implementation is split into cohesive packages or subfolders with
  visible ownership, not a sprawling flat file set or meaningless nesting.
- Descriptive, sufficiently verbose filenames identify module responsibility.
  Platform-required names and locations are preserved when genuinely
  required.
- JSON, YAML, TOML and other owned source assets belong in the owning
  module's local `assets/` folder unless a platform requires another name or
  location. Governed Atom carriers, Journals and Runtime outputs are not
  implementation source assets.

Under this proposal, size and cohesion rules are Method policy. The companion
Evaluation Draft specifies measurement, checker and linter paths; it does not
create, weaken or waive these rules. Existing CA-E-364 and CA-E-539 content
requires coordinated reconciliation at adoption, not reinterpretation now.

## Details

1. Count each standalone, nested, asynchronous and class-defined executable
   function or method by logical executable lines, excluding comments,
   docstrings and blanks. Count module physical lines as all text under the
   current convention. Exactly 25/40 and 200/300 remain within their
   respective limits; crossing a soft boundary requires a written cohesion
   review, while exceeding a hard boundary fails without exception.
2. Review the class responsibility separately from numeric size. Do not split
   a cohesive class merely to satisfy a number, and do not use a class-size
   argument to excuse an oversized or incohesive method.
3. Extract a helper only for a meaningful reusable responsibility or real
   boundary. Keep dependency direction visible and use cohesive packages or
   subfolders when a module grows. Avoid flat helper sprawl and arbitrary
   nesting.
4. Keep source assets beside their owning module under `assets/`, subject to
   genuine platform-required names or locations. Never reclassify governed
   Carriers, Journal records or Runtime outputs as local source assets.
5. Apply the policy to new or materially changed hand-authored source. Do not
   silently migrate vendor code, generated output, frozen fixtures or legacy
   history. A linked Evaluation result can be pass, fail or unresolved, but
   it is evidence about this Method rather than a second policy owner.

## Adoption notes

This Draft proposes Method ownership of the listed size, cohesion,
organization and asset decisions. It is not current authority and does not
silently supersede CA-M-403, CA-M-411, CA-M-419, CA-E-364 or CA-E-539.
Those active Atoms remain unchanged until coordinated adoption reconciles
their existing rules. The proposed Evaluation checks this Method rather than
owning a second set of rules.

Companion Evaluation Draft: [source-size and organization Evaluation](../../06_evaluation/draft/CA-E-draft-PROGRAMMATIC-GENERAL-EVALUATION_APPROACH--evaluate-source-size-cohesion-and-package-organization.md).

# Summary

Write RMED owner citations only at module start

## Scope

The method for materializing direct RMED-to-implementation traceability in
PROGRAMMATIC and descendant modules. It applies to actual implementation
owners, not to callers, facades, generated output, vendor code, frozen
fixtures, or legacy history unless those sources are explicitly admitted.

## Claim

Resolve current applicable RMED authority and the actual owner first, then
write exactly one readable `# implementation of:` block at the beginning of
each owning module. Do not write ownership blocks before functions, classes,
methods, or other implementation units. Use canonical Atom IDs only, preserve
the Requirement/Method/Evaluation/Delivery role distinction, choose the
narrowest applicable leaf in each branch, and keep independent branches
separate. Many-to-many ownership remains valid when each relation is
materially real.

A shared policy provider cites the Method that it actually defines and
implements. A consumer that merely imports, calls or decorates that provider
does not cite the policy Method solely for reuse. Find such consumers
mechanically through code references; do not create a second manual
`applies` graph. A module with other substantive RMED claims still cites
those own claims. If another module independently implements the policy
behavior, it is also an owner and cites the policy Method without duplicating
citations for mere reuse.

A test module is an Evaluation owner only when it materially implements the
Evaluation check, fixture, or verification behavior. A test that merely
exercises another module is not an owner of that module's Requirement,
Method, or Evaluation. The policy still applies wherever applicable whether
or not a citation is present, and a comment never proves conformance,
completion, or observed outcome.

## Details

1. Resolve current active RMED source and identify the module that materially
   realizes each claim. Select the narrowest directly realized leaf for every
   relevant `child_of` or `parent_of` branch and do not duplicate
   ancestors already covered by that leaf. Cite independent branches
   separately. Preserve uncertainty for unresolved or dynamic definitions and
   references; do not invent an owner, parent, policy or proof.
2. Write this exact shape at the module beginning. These IDs are illustrative,
   not asserted source links:

   ```text
   # implementation of:
   # Requirement: CA-R-123, CA-R-456
   # Method: CA-M-789
   # Evaluation: CA-E-012
   # Delivery: CA-D-345
   ```

   Use only canonical Atom IDs. Omit empty roles. Do not include versions,
   paths, titles, draft markers or an `applies` block. Do not add a second
   authored block before a function, class, method or unit.
3. For an error-handling decorator, retry policy, logging policy or similar
   cross-cutting rule, cite the module where the policy is defined and
   implemented. Mere callers, importers and decorators are consumers, not
   Method owners solely because they reuse it. Inspect actual definitions and
   mechanics, not imports alone. If a consumer contains independent RMED
   behavior, cite that behavior's own canonical roles.
4. Derive consumer/call-site references mechanically for review. Do not turn
   those references into authored ownership edges or a second manual
   `applies` graph. Comments are trace metadata only; authoritative Atoms
   and observed implementation evidence remain required. Keep Requirements
   as what must be done and Methods as how the implementation and citation
   format are written; linked Evaluation carriers check the result and do not
   redefine this Method.

5. Apply the method only to the admitted current implementation boundary.
   Report out-of-boundary files for explicit disposition rather than
   mass-editing them. A missing or ambiguous current branch, an
   unidentifiable owner, or an invalid block is a traceability gap: preserve
   the source and report the gap.

## Adoption notes

This Draft proposes the module-only traceability and owner-localization
correction. Current CA-R-2117, CA-M-431, CA-E-653 and CA-M-411 remain active
authority until a reviewed role correction or replacement is accepted and
promoted. This Draft specifies how to achieve the companion Requirement's
traceability outcome; it does not silently supersede current Atoms and is not
an implementation or release gate.

Companion Requirement Draft: [trace RMED claims to canonical implementation owners](../../04_requirement/draft/CA-R-draft-PROGRAMMATIC-GENERAL-REQUIREMENT--trace-rmed-claims-to-canonical-module-owners.md).

Companion Evaluation Draft: [owner-only module citations and derived call-site traces](../../06_evaluation/draft/CA-E-draft-PROGRAMMATIC-STANDARD-QA_CASE--verify-owner-only-module-citations-and-derived-call-site-traces.md).

declared rules. The Evaluation returns pass, fail or unresolved evidence; it
does not own independent thresholds, exceptions or interpretations. Unknown or

  nested function and classmethod independently using the resolved Method
  measurement profile. Never count a whole class as one function or use class

# Summary

Verify owner-only module citations and derived call-site traces

## Scope

New or materially changed admitted PROGRAMMATIC source and its directly owned
tests, including shared policy or decorator modules and their consumer modules.
Resolve the bound Method traceability policy first, then run this QA check. It
does not require a per-function, per-class, or per-method RMED block, and it
does not accept an `applies` annotation as evidence.

## Claim

The checker derives its required citation shape from the bound Method policy.
For each applicable owner module, it parses one current module-header
`# implementation of:` block, validates Atom IDs and role lines, verifies the
source and current carrier for each citation, selects the narrowest active
leaf for each applicable branch, and rejects an ancestor duplicated by that
leaf. A module header is the ownership unit; a per-unit block is neither
required nor used to establish completion.

A shared policy or decorator module cites the Method that it implements. A
consumer that only imports, calls, or decorates with that shared policy is not
the implementation owner of that Method and does not receive a duplicate
authored Method citation merely because a code reference exists. The checker
derives the provider/consumer code graph, verifies the actual decorator or
delegation mechanism rather than imports alone, and applies the Method's
owner-only and consumer-exception rules. A caller that owns independent claim
logic cites its own relevant roles; if it directly implements the policy
behavior elsewhere, the result is reviewed for duplicate ownership.

## Details

### Test case

Run an isolated fixture matrix containing:

1. a shared policy provider with a valid module-header Method citation;
2. a consumer that imports and calls the provider;
3. a consumer with an unused policy import;
4. a module missing the required decorator or delegation;
5. an unrelated consumer that references a different policy;
6. an independent policy owner with its own claim logic; and
7. a dynamic or unknown policy reference that cannot be resolved mechanically.

For every fixture, obtain the bound Method's role-ID parsing, source-validity,
provider/consumer graph, and test/evaluation-owner exception rules before
checking the result. The checker returns each measured citation, resolved
owner, applicable leaf, source evidence and test evidence; it reports an
unknown or unavailable Method rule as unresolved rather than substituting a
Requirement or an unrelated Evaluation.

The provider and consumers must be checked for actual decorator or delegation
behavior, not only imports or call-site syntax. A correctly cited module with
no per-function, per-class, or per-method block passes this owner-only case. A
new per-unit block in the obsolete or stale format is reported as a
traceability gap and must not crash runtime evaluation. Derive call-site
references mechanically for review; do not convert them into authored
ownership edges.

Reject malformed or incomplete cases containing an invalid or stale Atom ID,
version marker, path, filename title, wrong role citation, or archived Atom.
Calls are not proof that a policy was applied, comments are not proof of
conformance, and an unknown or dynamic reference is reported truthfully as
unresolved rather than treated as a complete call graph.

### Acceptance

Pass only when every assessed owner module has one valid current module-header
block, every citation resolves to the named current role, narrowest active
branches are selected without ancestor duplication, and the provider/consumer
matrix distinguishes implementation ownership from derived references. The
policy is accepted across all required modules only when the real decorator or
delegation mechanism is present; an import, call, comment, or relation alone
does not pass. Independent claim owners retain their own claim citations, and
many-to-many ownership is accepted when each localized module or package
relationship is substantive and unambiguous.

### Failure disposition

Report each missing, invalid, stale, overbroad, wrong-role, duplicate, or
unresolved citation and reject the affected traceability result. Preserve the
implementation and do not invent a call-graph edge, silently add an authored
citation, mass-edit source, or turn this Evaluation into a runtime failure.
Dynamic resolution remains unresolved until evidence identifies the owner and
the actual policy mechanism.

## Adoption notes

CA-E-653 and CA-R-2117 remain current context until a coordinated authority
revision is accepted; CA-R-2117 is informational here, not the rule source.
This Draft specifies a checker for the bound Method trace policy and does not
change those Atoms or claim current conformance. On promotion, the checker
must consume the promoted Method's own citation rules and retain unresolved
human-review results instead of treating a mechanically incomplete call graph
as complete.

Evaluated Method Draft: [module-start owner citations](../../05_method/draft/CA-M-draft-PROGRAMMATIC-STANDARD-ENG_DECISION--write-rmed-owner-citations-only-at-module-start.md).

active runtime policy. Operational evaluation requires the admitted Method;
historical CA-M-431 and CA-M-411 references are reconciliation context only.

# Summary

Declare the Node branch and derive the graph from Formal Claims

## Question

How should the graph model, Declaration Forms and notation change so that one coherent source declares each Node without repeated inherited definitions or ambiguous constraints?

## Scope

This proposal covers governing Drafts for the Node branch, graph Relations and notation, Role/Form naming, carrier mappings and formal Scope. It records the latest human decisions; earlier conflicting alternatives are superseded. The [Epic successor Draft](../../../../../03_plan/draft/CA-P-2694@39-draft-EPIC--entity-graph-refactor-stage-4-polishing.md) tracks adoption and implementation dependencies.

Actual Workflow, Step, Substep and Action instance review/migration is deferred by the latest Operator instruction. This pass reviews their model declarations and constraints; model-level examples do not perform instance review.

## Approach

Write the governing Drafts directly, keep the design rationale here, and review the packet before adoption. Preserve Current sources and completed publication history. Resolve exact source-to-Node mappings before replacing Definitions; never replace all `/` edges with composition.

## Results

### What changes

- **Carrier placement is explicit.** Use `@Carrier//Markdown file`. Deliver non-Content Objects into frontmatter. Deliver Content descendants into Markdown. Frontmatter is delimited YAML at the beginning of the file. Carrier filename/location are properties; location is repository-relative.
- **Node scope is explicit.** `Node/**, .**` selects narrower entities plus their Properties. Add `Node` when a rule also covers the root.

- **Names and values use separate expressions.** `p{:0..1}: [format]{:1}` separates occurrence from values. `p.*[...]` constrains immediate names. `p.**[...]` constrains names recursively. Expressions use semicolons.
- **Claim is one Property.** Keep `Atom.Content.Claim`. Formal content is an optional CFEL fence inside its Markdown value. No separate Formal Claim Property is retained. RMED Claim is required. Claim Scope, Semantics and Details are optional.
- **Delivery specifies representation.** `>>` delivers Objects to a referenced Carrier or its parts. Object means Node instance. Filename/location formula details remain separate until expressible.

- **Analysis is freeform.** `Atom.Content.**[string]{:0+}: [markdown]{:1}` constrains each dependent Property recursively. Sibling names are unique. `x.y.z` differs from `x.z`. Shared Atom constraints remain inherited.

- **Graph Syntax becomes CFEL — CAPRMEDIO Formal Expression Language.** CFEL covers expression syntax and meaning for Subject addresses and Formal Claims. Graph, CFEL and Carrier remain distinct model components. This names the existing language; it does not add notation.

- **Declaration is a Form of Requirement.** Use `Role: Requirement / Form: Declaration` and the existing R prefix. Within each selected effective MODEL, each declared member selected by `(Node, Node/**, .**)`, including Properties, has one effective Current Declaration with one matching active Subject. Count only those Declarations; other RMED may address the same Node. Use CFEL Formal Claims where possible. Use Claim prose only for constraints CFEL cannot express. Keep brief Semantics for Primary Nodes only. Each Property Declaration specifies two contracts: direct-value format/cardinality; dependent-entity format/cardinality. Unchanged inherited Properties reuse their original Declaration; explicit MODEL overrides select their local replacement. CFEL entities retain a Claim and may have Semantics.
- **Use Role and Form.** Rename Content Role to Role and the Role-specific Type to Form. These names express different purposes. Naming Methods prefer words that convey the actual distinction and reuse canonical expressions consistently; they do not impose a blanket word ban on useful contextual uses of `content`, `entity` or `type`.
- **Use two root kinds.** MODEL and PROJECT STRUCTURE are Primary Node kinds declared in CAPRMEDIO's self-describing MODEL. Their instance roots are `MODEL//CAPRMEDIO`, `PROJECT STRUCTURE//CAPRMEDIO`, and the corresponding consumer Project roots. The consumer MODEL is optional. PROJECT STRUCTURE describes Scope Structure, Aspects and other declared components. Core Meta-Model contains the Atoms defining CAPRMEDIO's MODEL. Extensible axis configuration stays deferred.
- **Declare Scope outside the constrained Unit.** State permitted active/passive Subjects and Relation endpoints/cardinalities. ENGINE's proposed Scope permits allowed instances and implementation RMED; model definitions use their declared model-defining Scope. A local MODEL does not automatically widen ENGINE's Scope. Target Scope never grants wider authority.
- **Keep graph meanings distinct.** `/` narrows Primary Nodes with inheritance, `//` names their instances, `.` addresses Properties, `+>`/`<+` expresses composition, and `>|`/`|<` expresses classification. Composition uses canonical IS_CONTAINED_BY and derived CONTAINS; Container has yes/no value cases. `(Node, Node/**, .**)` includes the root, its recursive narrower branch and their recursive Properties. `@` references an existing target, parentheses group, and `in (...)` states membership. `:` denotes an allowed value, `=` tests, and `==` establishes a required/derived conclusion. In Subjects, `:=` combines allowed value and condition, as in `Atom/(.Role := Method)`. It does not write an instance value or exclude other allowed values from Atom.Role. Formal Claims keep `:` and `=` separate. Full Formal Claims stay out of Subjects; `..` and an invented `::` meaning are excluded.
- **Keep both counts.** Relation cardinality constrains both written directions; reversal swaps the counts. Property syntax uses separate expressions for occurrence, direct values and immediate dependent names: `p{:occurrence count}; p: [value format]{:value count}; p.*[name format]{:child count}`. YAML and Markdown mappings preserve that distinction, including mixed section content and nested headings.
- **Derive Primary Node versus Property.** The Node branch permits zero or one IS_PROPERTY_OF bearer. Zero derives Primary Node and no direct value; one derives Property and forbids narrowing and instantiation. Property-bearing must be acyclic. HAS_VALUE binds a Property on an instance to a literal, such as CA-P-123.version = 1; literals do not become declared graph Nodes.
- **Inheritance supplies effective rules.** Narrower instances receive applicable Relation cardinalities and declared Property constraints. Do not redeclare an inherited Property or create a new Declaration merely for an inherited lookup. Each Node's single effective Declaration in the selected MODEL resolves its Relation whitelist, endpoint constraints and counts. MODEL inheritance may replace any inherited rule through an explicit local override; unchanged Declarations are reused. Inheritance neither copies instance facts nor gives a Property a second bearer.
- **Operations use siblings and explicit composition.** Workflow, Step, Substep and Action narrow Operations. Each Workflow has one or more Steps, each Step one Workflow. A Step exclusively runs one Action or contains one or more Substeps. Each Substep has one Step and runs one Action. Actions may have zero or more callers. RUN bindings do not establish execution evidence.
- **Store authored instance Relations once.** Rename Subject links to active/passive; store modeled authored Node-instance links under `relations`, with typed containment references. Derive HAS_ACTIVE_SUBJECT from the dedicated Subject field and derive inverse views. The exact Assignee/Target reference migration remains open.

Relation Definitions now state allowed Host/Target signatures and reuse `Direct ((HAS_INVERSE)) Derived`. Inverse views have no separate Definition Atom. Repeated migration commentary is removed from the governing Drafts.

### Why these changes

The human rationale is to remove words that add no useful distinction, keep each complete expression precise, and avoid defining inherited material repeatedly. Primary Nodes, Properties, narrowing, composition and classification need different meanings so the graph can express constraints faithfully. A formal Scope outside its Unit makes the Unit's permitted authority explicit. One Declaration gathers a Node's structure and permissions; formal rules support graph reconstruction without turning an address into a second programming language. Syntax explanations remain useful where symbols are not self-explanatory.

### MODEL and PROJECT STRUCTURE — latest architecture

The two kinds are declared in MODEL//CAPRMEDIO itself. The named Subject roots are their instances:

```text
MODEL//CAPRMEDIO
PROJECT STRUCTURE//CAPRMEDIO
    <+ Scope Structure
    <+ Aspects

MODEL//<PROJECT NAME>              (optional)
PROJECT STRUCTURE//<PROJECT NAME>
    <+ Scope Structure
    <+ Aspects
```

The Project name above is a placeholder. A Project uses MODEL//CAPRMEDIO. It may define a local MODEL. A local MODEL inherits MODEL//CAPRMEDIO and may override any inherited rule. No inherited rule requires an overridable marker.

One Current authoritative Declaration per Node means one effective Declaration within the selected MODEL. Unchanged inherited Declarations are reused. A local replacement and its base source can coexist without becoming two effective owners in that MODEL. This selection context is distinct from the Project-wide instance context used by UNIQUE.

Core Meta-Model is a Scope Unit in CAPRMEDIO's Scope Structure. It contains the governing Atoms defining MODEL//CAPRMEDIO, including the two root kinds. This self-description does not identify the MODEL instance with its Scope Unit or PROJECT STRUCTURE instance. Existing ordered Scope Unit proposals remain subject to exact registration and mapping.

Model inheritance connects MODEL instances. It is separate from `/` Node narrowing and `<+` containment. The inheritance Relation name and exact Model-selection/override binding still need specification; this pass adds no invented notation or runtime behavior.

This replaces the earlier owner-wrapper layout and the MODEL-versus-PROJECT root split. The rationale is to distinguish reusable declarations from each Project's actual structure, reuse inherited material, and let each local MODEL control all of its effective rules.

Declare the Node branch and derive the graph from Formal Claims

## Question

How should the graph model, Declaration Forms and notation change so that one coherent source declares each Node without repeated inherited definitions or ambiguous constraints?

## Scope

- **Claim is one Property.** Keep `Atom.Content.Claim`. Formal content is an optional CFEL fence inside its Markdown value. No separate Formal Claim Property is retained. RMED Claim is required. Claim Scope, Semantics and Details are optional.

Within each selected effective MODEL, each declared member selected by `(Node, Node/**, .**)`, including Properties, has one effective Current Declaration with one matching active Subject. Count only those Declarations; other RMED may address the same Node. Use CFEL Formal Claims where possible. Use Claim prose only for constraints CFEL cannot express. Unchanged inherited Properties reuse their original Declaration; explicit MODEL overrides select their local replacement. CFEL entities retain a Claim and may have Semantics.
